IFN‐γ–JAK/STAT Axis: A Potential Inflammatory Signaling Module in SD‐ILD
evidence_snippets: Macrophages are well‐established cellular responders to IFN‐γ–JAK/STAT signaling. IFN‐γ can promote STAT1‐dependent transcriptional programs associated with macrophage activation, enhanced antigen‐presentation capacity, and increased inflammatory mediator production [10].

Experimental studies further indicate that IFN‐γ can promote macrophage polarization toward a pro‐inflammatory phenotype, providing a potential mechanism through which macrophages may contribute to the persistence of inflammatory responses [44].
title: IFN‐γ‐Associated Signaling Networks in Interstitial Lung Disease Associated With Sjögren's Disease

evidence_snippets: Recent studies have identified upregulation of inflammatory cytokines, such as interferon gamma (IFN-γ), contributing to constitutive activation of the janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) signaling pathway in granulomatous diseases.3,4 Targeting this pathway with JAK inhibition provides a promising therapeutic approach to NL, supported by clinical success in granulomatous diseases such as sarcoidosis.3
title: Clinical improvement of necrobiosis lipoidica with topical ruxolitinib.
